subject: Dedicated capacity sizing / throughput model for Stargazer AI
messages:
From: Alex Jin <alex.jin@stargazer.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Lee <maya@stargazer.ai>, procurement@stargazer.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing request / p95 SLO targets

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — Stargazer is moving quickly and procurement asked us to get a dedicated sizing estimate from Redwood to include in our internal ROI/commit materials. High level:
- Current model: internal gen-2 instruction model (approx. 7B-ish) used for customer-facing chat; we call it "stg-gen-2"
- Baseline traffic today: ~18M tokens/day (avg), but expected to grow to ~120M tokens/day within 6 months after launch
- Peak shape: bursts up to ~2.8x daily average during US business hours; concurrency peaks expected 650–900 concurrent users at peak
- SLO target we need to model: p95 generation latency <= 300ms (client expects snappy chat) — procurement is also asking for an alternate p95 at 350ms for pricing tradeoffs

Can you help us with a tokens/sec mapping to GPU types (A100-80GB vs H100), recommended committed TPS for a Dedicated slab, and what realistic headroom we should plan for (safety factor)? I attached a CSV of our recent API metrics for reference (Stargazer_APIMetrics.csv).

Also, can Redwood run a 48-hour synthetic spike test on a pilot slab before we sign any commit?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Alex Jin
Head of Platform
Stargazer AI

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jin <alex.jin@stargazer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 17:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request / p95 SLO targets

Hi Alex — thanks for the data and context, this is exactly the sort of input we need. Looping in Ben (SE) and Priyom (capacity modeling) who will put together a short sizing model.

A few quick clarifying questions that will make the model tighter:
- Which model checkpoint / tokenizer are you using (we need approx input+output token split)?
- Typical generation length distribution (median output tokens, 95th output tokens)?
- Are you using streaming completions (we can factor tail latency impacts) or batched non-streaming?
- Any strict availability SLO (99.9 vs 99.95) that should feed into headroom assumptions?

We can push a draft estimate in 24 hours. If helpful, we can also propose a mutual action plan and a 48-hour pilot spike (we've done these before). I attached a short MAP template (mutual-action-plan.pdf) — we'll populate it with timelines and pilot criteria.

Would you be available for a 30m call tomorrow morning PST to walk through the CSV?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Alex Jin <alex.jin@stargazer.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing request / p95 SLO targets — draft throughput mapping

Hi team — pulled together a first-pass throughput/latency mapping based on the CSV and the assumptions below. Attaching a workbook with the calc steps (stargazer-throughput-draft.xlsx).

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model: stg-gen-2, tokenization ratio ~1.12 input->token, average generation length 64 tokens (median 32, p95 220)
- Streaming enabled (we'll assume client streams partial tokens)
- Typical prompt length 120 input tokens average
- Target p95 latency = 300ms (alternate scenario 350ms)

GPU performance knobs used:
- H100 (dense, with optimized kernels + quantization path): ~1400 tokens/sec single-GPU sustained (1-stream, low batch) at this model size
- A100-80GB (dense): ~900 tokens/sec single-GPU sustained
- With KV cache and prefix caching opportunities, effective sustained TPS can improve ~1.2x for sessions with reused context

Traffic mapping (sustained vs peak):
- 120M tokens/day -> average sustained ~1,389 tokens/sec (120,000,000 / 86,400)
- Peak burst factor 2.8 -> peak short spike ~3,889 tokens/sec
- Concurrency estimate aligns: 650–900 concurrent active sessions with streaming

Sizing guidance (recommendation):
- Baseline commit (predictable capacity): target committed sustained TPS = 2,000 tokens/sec (covers ~1.44x average; leaves room for short growth and reduces overage variability)
- Burst capacity: allow autoscale to handle up to 4,000 tokens/sec in short bursts (we can tie to burst credits or on-demand pricing)
- Mapping to GPUs: for the sustained committed TPS = 2,000
  - H100s: 2 x H100 (2 x 1400 = 2800 tokens/sec raw) -> with safety margin and process overhead recommend 2x for sustained + 1x spare (3 H100s total in pool)
  - A100-80GBs: 3 x A100 (3 x 900 = 2700 tokens/sec raw) -> recommend 3 active + 1 spare (4 total)

Headroom / safety factor: recommend a 40% headroom on top of committed sustained TPS to meet p95 under noisy neighbor and model variance. That leads to an operational target of ~2,800 tokens/sec effective for the 2,000 committed line.

Latency tradeoffs: moving from 300ms p95 to 350ms p95 reduces required GPU count by roughly one GPU in the A100 scenario because you can use slightly larger batch sizes and accept marginal token serialization delay. For H100 it buys ~15% more effective capacity. We'll include both scenarios in the workbook.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Use prefix/KV caching for conversational sessions — for Stargazer's traffic this could reduce upstream sustained token work by ~10–20% for repeated sessions
- Enable per-customer routing to Dedicated for high-volume customers and fallback to hosted smaller models during extreme surges
- Pilot spike: Redwood recommends a 48h synthetic spike with mirrored traffic at 120–150% of expected peak to validate autoscale and p95 under production-like queuing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm tokenizer/median and p95 tokens for more accurate mapping
2) Run 48h pilot on 3x A100 and 2x H100 candidate pools and measure real p95 at peak load
3) Lock in committed TPS and slab size in MAP and provide pricing delta for the two SLO options (300ms vs 350ms)

Happy to present the calc in a short run-through — suggest 30m today at 11:00 PST.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Jin <alex.jin@stargazer.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Lee <maya@stargazer.ai>, procurement@stargazer.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request / p95 SLO targets — draft throughput mapping

Thanks Ben and team — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications:
- Procurement is pushing hard for a p95 of 300ms (they've budgeted for higher commit) but engineering asks whether 350ms could be an acceptable fallback for a lower committed price. Can you quantify the price delta roughly between the two SLOs?
- We can confirm tokenizer details today (we use SentencePiece, rough tokens per request aligns with your assumptions).

We'd like Redwood to include a clear commit vs burst pricing example in the MAP so procurement can move quickly. Also — the pilot spike is acceptable, please include pass/fail criteria for p95 and error rates.

Best,
Alex

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jin <alex.jin@stargazer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request / p95 SLO targets — next steps and pilot

Alex — great, thanks for the quick reply. Action items and next steps: 

1) Ben / Priyom will finalize two MAP scenarios in the attached workbook (300ms vs 350ms), including: committed TPS, recommended GPU slab (A100 vs H100), expected tokens/day headroom, and estimated monthly commit pricing and burst rates.
2) We will populate pass/fail criteria for the 48-hour pilot:
   - p95 generation latency <= target SLO (300ms or 350ms depending on scenario) for >= 95% of 5-minute windows during the test
   - error rate <= 0.5% (5xx and request failures)
   - CPU/GPU thermal or OOM events = 0
3) We will run the 48-hour mirrored-synthetic spike at 150% of observed peak (~6,000 tokens/sec sustained for the test window) and provide the raw latency traces and token-by-token logs for your engineering team.
4) Draft MAP and pricing (including approximate price delta between SLO tiers) will be in your inbox by EOD Monday.

Link to shared MAP and test plan: https://redwood.example/ds/links/STG-1234
DocuSign envelope (standby): https://docusign.com/ENVELOPE/abc123

If procurement wants a quick sketch of pricing delta now: estimate is ~18–25% premium for the 300ms p95 path versus 350ms p95 (driven by extra reserved GPU capacity and burst credits). We will refine that number once we finalize the slab mapping.

I'll book the 30m run-through with Ben and Priyom for Monday morning PST — will send calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
